title: Flavour current correlators and the non-Abelian hydrodynamic approximation: the charged sector
authors: Thomas Apostolidis, Matti Järvinen, Elias Kiritsis, Francesco Nitti, Andrea Olzi, Edwan Préau
abstract: Flavor-current correlators are studied in strongly-coupled dense (holographic) matter, at finite quark chemical potential $μ_q$ and finite isospin asymmetry. The non-Abelian hydrodynamic description of the charged currents is derived in the presence of an isospin chemical potential $μ_3$. The two-point correlators of charged currents are then computed holographically at finite quark and isospin chemical potentials. In the near-extremal hydrodynamic regime, $ω, k, T, μ_3 \ll μ\equiv \sqrt{μ_q^2+μ_3^2}$, relevant for cold strongly coupled matter, the IR properties of the correlators are studied. It is shown that in this regime, the correlators agree with the non-Abelian hydrodynamic predictions. Therefore, the traditional regime of validity of standard hydrodynamics extends beyond $ω, k \ll T \ll μ$ to the so-called extended hydrodynamic regime $T\ll ω, k \ll μ$. The holographic product formula is applied to the present non-Abelian system, and is used to propose an extended hydrodynamic approximation capturing both hydrodynamic-like poles and the leading effect of AdS$_2$ poles, by resumming the low-$ω$ logarithms. The results are verified through a detailed numerical analysis of the exact correlators and quasi-normal mode spectrum.
summary: This paper studies flavor current correlators in dense, strongly-coupled matter using holographic methods. It derives and verifies an extended hydrodynamic approximation that extends the known validity range of standard hydrodynamics. The findings are crucial for accurately modeling transport properties in cold, highly asymmetric quantum systems.
main_problem: The study investigates flavor-current correlators in strongly-coupled, dense matter under conditions of finite quark chemical potential ($\mu_q$) and isospin asymmetry ($\mu_3$). The goal is to extend the applicability of hydrodynamic descriptions into non-standard regimes.
main_result: The authors show that the standard hydrodynamics validity extends to an extended regime ($T \ll \omega, k \ll \mu$), where correlators match non-Abelian hydrodynamic predictions. They propose a new approximation using the holographic product formula to capture both hydrodynamic and $	ext{AdS}_2$ pole effects.
method: The research employs holographic methods (holographic duality) to compute two-point correlators of charged currents in the bulk, deriving non-Abelian hydrodynamics for the boundary theory. Results are verified through numerical analysis of exact correlators and quasi-normal mode spectra.
model_or_system: The system is strongly-coupled dense matter (relevant for neutron stars), modeled holographically using a five-dimensional Einstein-Yang-Mills theory. The physics involves charged currents governed by non-Abelian dynamics due to the presence of an isospin chemical potential ($\mu_3$).
key_observables: Two-point correlators of charged currents, quasi-normal mode (QNMs) spectrum.
important_parameters: Quark chemical potential ($\mu_q$), isospin asymmetry ($\mu_3$), temperature ($T$), and wave vector/frequency ($\omega, k$). The analysis focuses on the near-extremal regime where $\omega, k, T \ll \mu$.
main_assumptions: The primary assumptions involve using holographic duality to model strongly coupled matter and assuming validity in specific low-energy regimes (near-extremal/extended hydrodynamic).
paper_structure: The paper first derives the non-Abelian hydrodynamic description for charged currents. It then computes the two-point correlators holographically at finite chemical potentials, demonstrating agreement with hydrodynamics in the near-extremal regime. Finally, it applies the holographic product formula to propose an extended approximation and verifies results numerically.
why_interesting: This work extends hydrodynamic descriptions into regimes previously thought inaccessible, providing theoretical tools for understanding non-equilibrium dynamics in extreme astrophysical environments like neutron stars, which is a key area of modern statistical physics.
